article_title: Investigation of Conceptual Change about Double-Slit Interference in Secondary School Physics
citation: Mustafa Sabri Kocakulah, Mehmet Kural. (2010). Investigation of conceptual change about double-slit interference in secondary school physics. International Journal of Environmental & Science Education. http://www.ijese.com/
title: Yip's three-source taxonomy of students' science misconceptions
description: The article adopts Yip's (1998) classification of students' misconceptions in science after teaching by the nature and origin of their sources into three broad groups: informal ideas generated through life experiences that students bring to class; misconceptions developed during teaching, defined as "incomplete or improper views" arising from missing prerequisite knowledge; and instructional misconceptions originating from teachers and textbooks. The article uses this taxonomy to frame why student ideas resist instruction and how teaching should be designed to remedy them. It states that "Yip (1998) categorizes students‟ misconceptions in science after teaching according to the nature and sources of origin into three broad grou ps."
requirements: Identification of misconceptions and monitoring the development of informal views are needed to construct effective teaching strategies that remedy them
constraints: The taxonomy applies to misconceptions present after teaching, categorized by the nature and sources of their origin
target_learners: science students in secondary and university education
target_learning_goals: replacing misconceptions with scientific conceptions in physics topics such as the wave model of light
examples: The article cites Kousathana, Demerouti and Tsaparlis (2005) terming the teacher- and textbook-origin category instructional misconceptions and suggesting inclusion of history of science in instruction
